cards.text: Jeremiah, a prophet to Judah, has just heard the LORD say Jerusalem will become a heap of rubble (Jeremiah 9:11). Now a question goes out: who is wise enough to understand this? Why is the land destroyed and scorched like a desert, so no one can pass through it?

cards.question: Someone answers the question of why the land is destroyed. The ___ answers.
Why does the LORD say the land of Judah is destroyed?

answers.text: They forsook His law and did not obey His voice
They lost too many battles to their enemies
They let their fields go unplanted for years

cards.text: Instead, the LORD says, they followed the stubbornness of their hearts. That's your phone's GPS saying turn left, and you turning right AGAIN because you 'know a shortcut.'

cards.question: Following their stubborn hearts, who did the people go after?
The LORD says the people came up with chasing the Baals all on their own, with nobody teaching them.

cards.text: So the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says He will feed this people wormwood and give them poisoned water to drink.

cards.question: The LORD also says He will scatter the people. Where?

answers.text: Among nations they have never known
Among the cities of the Philistines

cards.text: And He will send a sword after them until He has finished them off. This is where the stubborn road ends.
Then the LORD of Hosts says to take note and summon the wailing women. Not just any of them, either: send for the most skillful.

cards.question: The LORD says of the wailing women, 'Let them come quickly and take up a lament over us…' What is that lament meant to bring?

cards.text: Then the sound of wailing is heard from Zion: 'How devastated we are! How great is our shame!…' I bet that's a sound you don't forget.

cards.question: In the wailing heard from Zion, the cry is that they have abandoned the land because their dwellings have been torn down.

cards.text: Now the women are told to open their ears to the word of the LORD. They're to teach their daughters to wail, and one another to lament.

cards.question: Here's the reason for all the wailing. ___ has climbed in through the windows and entered the fortresses.

cards.text: Death has come in to cut off the children from the streets and the young men from the town squares. I think this one hurts.
Then comes the word of the LORD: the corpses of men will fall like dung on the open field, like newly cut grain behind the reaper.

cards.question: The LORD says someone will come along behind and gather up the fallen.

cards.text: Then the LORD says not to let the wise man boast in his wisdom, or the strong man in his strength. Friend, I shared a junk drawer with dead batteries who argued all day about who had the most charge left, and not one of them could run a TV remote.

cards.question: There's a third man on the list too. The LORD says he shouldn't boast in his ___.
So if someone is going to boast, what does the LORD say to boast in?

answers.text: That he understands and knows the LORD
That he keeps every rule perfectly
That he gives more than his neighbors

cards.text: He's the One to know: the LORD, who exercises loving devotion, justice and righteousness on the earth. Wisdom? Strength? Riches? Nah, friend. THAT'S the brag.

cards.question: The LORD says loving devotion, justice and righteousness are things He puts up with but doesn't delight in.

cards.text: Then the LORD says, 'Behold, the days are coming,' when He will punish all who are circumcised only in the flesh.

cards.question: Judah is on the LORD's list of those circumcised only in the flesh whom He will punish, right alongside Egypt, Edom, Ammon and Moab.

cards.text: So are all the inhabitants of the desert who clip the hair of their temples. And the LORD says all these nations are uncircumcised.

cards.question: And the whole house of Israel? The LORD says they are uncircumcised in ___.
